title: The Story Behind the ‘not’
paragraphs: A little server history for anyone who has ever wondered why some of us have "not" sitting in front of our names.
It started with basically nothing. When I first joined Discord, I had no idea what I was doing. No decorations, no gimmicks, no carefully crafted username — just my first name, plain and exposed.

One of my very first nights on Discord, I ended up in a voice chat with someone who was having a rough trip on psychedelics. I stayed with them, talked them through it, and when the night ended, that was pretty much that. We didn’t really speak again.

Months later, they recognized me in another chat and thanked me. Someone joked that I should be crowned the server’s official trip sitter — the person people could count on when things got heavy. I laughed it off and said something along the lines of: "Good luck finding me next time. I’ll just change my name."
And then the joke stuck. When we eventually built out the original server, the "not" prefix caught on. What started as a throwaway joke slowly became something a little bigger.

It became a small symbol of a larger idea: this was supposed to be a place where you didn’t have to hide behind a username. You didn’t need to be anonymous just to protect yourself from a room full of strangers, because ideally, the people here weren’t strangers anymore. They were people you actually knew. People you could trust.
The "not" was never really about denial. It was about taking the mask off. A quiet way of saying: "I don’t need to hide who I am here."

So, is it required? Not at all. Pun fully intended. It isn’t a rule and it isn’t an obligation. It’s just a small piece of server history that you’re welcome to carry if it means something to you. Some people wear it. Some don’t. Either way is completely fine.
But if you ever feel like adding a little piece of the server’s history to your name, feel free to put a "not" in front of it. And now you know why.

title: Why the Server Is Called Chairs
paragraphs: Alright, part two of the lore dump. This one is about the name of the server itself: Chairs.

First, let’s get one thing out of the way: I did not invent "chairs" as a substitute for "cheers." That one isn’t mine. It has been floating around the internet for a long time, and the exact origin is murky enough that if you ask five different people, you’ll probably get five different answers.

My first real exposure to it was on r/cripplingalcoholism — which, for the record, I was mostly reading because the stories were entertaining. If you’ve ever spent time there, you probably know the sign-off. People would end posts with "chairs" instead of "cheers."

It was a little bit of linguistic drift that turned into a kind of ritual — a nod to sobriety, or the lack of it, surviving another day, and the messy human experience the community was built around. It wasn’t exactly just a joke. It carried a little weight.
I borrowed it. I started dropping "chairs" into Discord the same way, and eventually it worked its way into everything I was doing. It even ended up in line calls.

For a couple of months, it became a small thing among friends. Never some massive meme, just a little inside joke that somehow lasted longer than most. So when it eventually came time to build my own server, the name wasn’t really much of a decision. It just was.

Chairs had already become something connected to me personally — a word with its own history attached to my name and the people around me. Using anything else would have felt like starting over when we already had something that meant something.

That’s really the whole story. Borrowed from a corner of the internet I have a lot of respect for, carried around for a while, slowly turned into an inside joke, and eventually became the name hanging over our own front door. Chairs.

title: The Story of Angrier Jordan
paragraphs: Alright, last one. Part three of three. If you’ve made it through all of the lore, congratulations — you now officially know more server history than some people who have been around for months. This last one is the origin story of our bot: Angrier Jordan.

The Backstory: You have to understand something about past me. I know it may be hard to imagine now, but back in the day I had a bit of a temper. A genuine short fuse. I was blunt to a fault, said exactly what I thought with basically zero filter, and once I made up my mind about something, that was usually the end of the conversation. Decision made. You could bring me a mountain of evidence and I’d still be capable of responding with: "Cool. Still no."

It became such a well-known thing about me that the staff team on the original server, The Dome, turned it into a running joke. Meetings, group chats, voice calls — somebody would eventually bring it up.

The Alt Account: One day, one particular staff member — who is staying anonymous forever because they earned that right — decided to take the joke one step further. They made an alt account. They joined The Dome. And they named it: Angier Jordan. Say it out loud a couple of times. Angier Jordan. Angrier Jordan. There it is. That was the entire joke. And it was aimed directly at me. With love. Probably.

The Mystery: What made it work was that almost nobody knew who was actually behind the account. Only two or three people were ever let in on the secret. Everyone else had a theory. People would DM me convinced they had cracked the case. Staff would speculate in voice chat. Someone was always "pretty sure" they knew who it was. And every single time, they were wrong. The account outlived every theory anybody came up with. For years.

The Bit: The account committed to the joke completely. Someone posts a huge exciting announcement? Angier Jordan appears with something dry and completely unimpressed. Someone is hyped about an event or a giveaway? Angier Jordan shows up to rain on the parade — or, more accurately, personally piss in their Cheerios. No exceptions. If there was a good mood in the room, Angier Jordan’s job was to lower it slightly. That consistency was honestly the entire charm of the character.

The Legacy: The account stayed active until I left The Dome late last year. By then, Angier Jordan wasn’t really just a joke anymore. It had become part of the furniture. A legitimate piece of the server’s culture and history, whether people knew the full story behind it or not.

So when it came time to name the bot for Chairs, there wasn’t much of a debate. Bringing the character back just made sense. Same energy. Same attitude. Same commitment to being mildly annoyed by everyone’s happiness. Except now, instead of being a person hiding behind an alt account, it’s a bot. Which, if anything, feels like a promotion. Welcome back, Angrier Jordan.
